title: Environment HDR Probe Shared Between Two GLB Showcase Objects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN import map for 'three' and 'three/addons/') that showcases two GLB models under a shared environment HDR probe with full interactive material controls.

## Scene Setup
- Use a WebGLRenderer with toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping, toneMappingExposure = 1.0, outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace, and antialias enabled. Set background to a dark grey (0x1a1a2e).
- Create a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 5) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls from addons.
- Use RGBELoader (from 'three/addons/loaders/RGBELoader.js') to load an equirectangular HDR environment. Since no real HDR file is available, GENERATE a procedural environment map using THREE.PMREMGenerator: create a small scene with a hemisphere light (sky=0x88ccff, ground=0x443322) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 2, position (3,5,2)), then use pmremGenerator.fromScene() to produce the envMap texture. Assign this envMap to scene.environment so all PBR materials receive it.
- Add a subtle ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.3) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.5) at (5, 10, 5) for fill.
- Load 'InterpolationTest.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place it at position (-2, 0, 0). Scale uniformly so its bounding box longest axis is ~1.5 units. Label it 'Model A'.
- Load 'ScatteringSkull.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place it at position (2, 0, 0). Scale uniformly so its bounding box longest axis is ~1.5 units. Label it 'Model B'.
- After loading each model, traverse all meshes and store original material properties (roughness, metalness, envMapIntensity, color) for undo.
- Add a ground plane (PlaneGeometry 20x20, MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 0.8, metalness 0.1, color 0x333344) rotated -PI/2 on X at y=0.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose and continuously update:
- modelALoaded: boolean
- modelBLoaded: boolean
- envMapApplied: boolean (true once pmrem envMap is set on scene.environment)
- envMapIntensity: number (current envMapIntensity applied to all model meshes, default 1.0)
- roughnessOffset: number (offset added to all mesh roughness values, default 0.0, clamped so final roughness stays 0..1)
- metalnessOverride: number or null (null = use original, otherwise override all meshes, range 0..1)
- toneMappingExposure: number (renderer.toneMappingExposure)
- selectedModel: 'A' | 'B' | 'none' (which model is selected for per-model operations)
- modelAVisible: boolean
- modelBVisible: boolean
- modelAEnvIntensity: number (per-model envMapIntensity for A)
- modelBEnvIntensity: number (per-model envMapIntensity for B)
- rotationSpeed: number (auto-rotation speed in radians/sec for both models on Y axis, default 0.0)
- wireframeMode: boolean (default false)
- undoStack: array of state snapshot names (strings)
- undoStackLength: number
- backgroundMode: 'solid' | 'envmap' (whether scene.background is solid color or the envMap)
- modelAPosition: {x, y, z}
- modelBPosition: {x, y, z}
- meshCountA: number (total mesh count in model A)
- meshCountB: number (total mesh count in model B)

## HUD / UI
Create a DOM overlay panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text, 280px wide) with:
1. Title: 'HDR Probe Showcase'
2. A slider labeled 'Env Intensity' (range 0..3, step 0.1, default 1.0) — sets global envMapIntensity on ALL meshes of both models.
3. A slider labeled 'Roughness Offset' (range -1..1, step 0.05, default 0) — adds offset to each mesh's original roughness (clamped 0..1).
4. A slider labeled 'Metalness Override' (range 0..1, step 0.05) with a checkbox 'Enable Metalness Override' (unchecked by default). When unchecked, metalnessOverride = null and original values used.
5. A slider labeled 'Exposure' (range 0.1..5, step 0.1, default 1.0) — sets renderer.toneMappingExposure.
6. A slider labeled 'Rotation Speed' (range 0..3, step 0.1, default 0) — auto-rotates both models around Y.
7. Two buttons: 'Select Model A' and 'Select Model B' — sets selectedModel state.
8. A button 'Toggle Wireframe' — toggles wireframeMode on all meshes.
9. A button 'Toggle Background' — switches backgroundMode between 'solid' and 'envmap'.
10. A button 'Toggle Model A Visibility' and 'Toggle Model B Visibility'.
11. A button 'Undo' — reverts the last material change from the undo stack.
12. Display text showing: selected model, current envMapIntensity, roughnessOffset, exposure, meshCountA, meshCountB.

## Interactions
- Keyboard '1': select Model A. Keyboard '2': select Model B. Keyboard '0': deselect.
- Keyboard 'W': toggle wireframe.
- Keyboard 'B': toggle background mode.
- Keyboard 'U': undo last change.
- Keyboard ArrowUp/ArrowDown: when a model is selected, adjust that model's per-model envMapIntensity by +/-0.1 (clamped 0..3). This overrides the global for that specific model.
- Keyboard 'R': reset all material properties to original values, clear roughnessOffset, metalnessOverride, set envMapIntensity to 1.0, exposure to 1.0.
- Every material change (slider or keyboard) pushes a snapshot name onto undoStack before applying.

## Undo System
- Before each material property change, push a descriptor string (e.g., 'envIntensity:1.0->1.5') onto undoStack and store the previous values.
- Undo pops the last entry and restores those values to all affected meshes.
- undoStackLength always reflects undoStack.length.

## Animation Loop
- Each frame: if rotationSpeed > 0, rotate both model root objects around Y by rotationSpeed * deltaTime.
- Update __3D_STATE__ every frame with current values.
- Ensure modelAPosition and modelBPosition reflect actual world positions of model roots.
physics_constraints: All material values must be clamped: roughness [0,1], metalness [0,1], envMapIntensity [0,3], toneMappingExposure [0.1,5]. No NaN values in any material property or position. Undo stack must be consistent — undo restores exact previous numerical values (epsilon < 0.001). Per-model envMapIntensity overrides must not affect the other model.
